messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: multivar norm problem's in Eigen triangularView()
parts:
Good news now (bad at the end). I fixed
the template syntax problem in multi_normal.
The key issue is that this won't compile:

template <typename T>
void
foo(Matrix<T,Dynamic,Dynamic>& L) {
L.triangularView<Eigen::Lower>();
}

Because of the . and < in the template, it turns
out you need to nudge the C++ parser a bit with
a hint (otherwise "L.triangularView" is parsed as
a member object and "<" as a binary operator):

template <typename T>
void
foo2(Matrix<T,Dynamic,Dynamic>& L) {
L.template triangularView<Eigen::Lower>();
}

Who knew?

I fixed multi_normal.hpp so that it compiles and
made a few other changes.

I renamed the second function to "multi_normal_cholesky_log".

I also replaced the template expression triangular view
argument with a regular old matrix, only the lower-triangular
portion of which will be used. Views aren't really meant
to be passed as arguments.

Two bits of bad news, though:

Compiling crashes clang++ on my Mac.

~/stan>clang++ -v
clang version 2.9 (tags/RELEASE_29/final)
Target: x86_64-apple-darwin10
Thread model: posix

2. It's not getting the value in the test.

I checked that everything's getting passed right
and the inverse and diffs are right. I don't
actually know the right formula, so I hope Ben
can debug it from here.

- Bob
